question.text: A Cat III AIF offers Class A1 (1.5% fee), A2 (2%), B1 (2%), C1 (2%). After one year, NAV differences BETWEEN Class A1 and others arise primarily due to:

answer.text: Differential management fee allocation in series calculations

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook's Series NAV tables show that management fees are allocated differentially across Classes A1, A2, B1 and C1, and that Class A1 ends up with the highest Series NAV precisely because it bears a lower management fee. The class-level fee difference is what drives the NAV gap. The Trap: Redemption patterns, currency moves and tax do not explain a structural NAV gap that arises directly from a different fee rate being charged to each class. Note: Based on Series-XIX-B workbook pp.289-293, which illustrates the differential management-fee allocation and the resulting higher Series NAV for Class A1.
